# Kern settings row — M3 guidance

<!-- Generated by apps/site/scripts/one-off/migrate-guidance.mjs. Do not edit by hand.
     The component pages carry the reference; this file carries the guidance. -->

## Web

### Features

Reach for the Kern settings row when a settings screen needs one labelled control: the one row contract pairing a label with a single trailing control. `control` picks the one — switch, segmented, select, button, or custom with a host-owned `trailing` slot — and there is never more than one control per row, because a second control is a second row. Each control kind carries its own state trio, controlled or uncontrolled, while selection state lives on the control kind that owns it — there is no row-level value. `label` is required because it names both the row and its control, with `supporting` carrying the explanatory line beneath, and icons arrive as registry nodes with badges marking button rows. Activation never nests: navigational rows activate on the whole row with a chevron while every other kind keeps activation on the trailing control, and navigation is the button kind's job alone.

## Native

### Features

Reach for the Kern settings row when a settings screen needs one labelled control: the one row contract pairing a label with a single trailing control — the native twin under the same contract. `control` picks the one — switch, segmented, select, button, or custom with a host-owned `trailing` slot — and there is never more than one control per row, because a second control is a second row. Each control kind carries its own state trio, controlled or uncontrolled, while selection state lives on the control kind that owns it — there is no row-level value. `label` is required because it names both the row and its control, with `supporting` carrying the explanatory line beneath. Segmented rows announce as a radiogroup of labelled options, select rows own a trigger driving the controlled sheet, and navigational rows activate on the whole row while every other kind keeps activation on the trailing control, so controls never nest.
